terms.comment: A description of ours, on the model of Morgan–Owens’s soda pistōria for baking soda: pistōrius is classical for what belongs to the baker (Cels., Plin.). We have found no word for baking paper in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Cato did the same work with oiled bay leaves laid under the cake; see the examples.

phrases.latin: Chartam pistōriam fōrmae subde, nē placenta haereat.
phrases.english: Put baking paper in the tin so the cake doesn’t stick.

phrases.latin: folia laurea ūncta suppōnitō, placentam fingitō
phrases.english: put oiled bay leaves underneath and shape the cake

phrases.latin: et ubi dēfīnxeris, laurī folia subtus additō, cum coquēs
phrases.english: and when you have shaped them, put bay leaves underneath when you bake them

sources: Lewis & Short: charta · Lewis & Short: pistorius
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. soda: baking soda.
